title: Pokémon Franchise Overview
body:
Pokémon began as video games developed by Game Freak and published by Nintendo, first released in Japan in 1996, and grew into an animated series, films, a card game and merchandise, all documented in public release records.

This public edition records only verifiable facts — game titles, developers, release years and formats — in original wording, with no copied game text, dialogue or lyrics.

The companion Signature edition is separate, labeled unofficial fiction with original trainers and creatures, and it claims no affiliation with or endorsement by Nintendo, Game Freak or The Pokémon Company.

How to use this record: start with the overview, then read the work-by-work records in publication order. Every date and credit below is a public fact; no copyrighted text is reproduced anywhere in this database.

title: Pokémon Reading and Viewing Order Guide
body:
Recommended public order for the works in this database is publication and release order, beginning with Pokémon Red and Green (Japan) (1996) and ending with Pokémon Scarlet and Violet (2022). That order follows how the franchise actually reached the public, and it avoids assuming any later reordering.

The full order is: Pokémon Red and Green (Japan) (1996); Pokémon (animated series) (1997); Pokémon Yellow (1998); Pokémon Gold and Silver (1999); Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire (2002); Pokémon Diamond and Pearl (2006); Pokémon X and Y (2013); Pokémon Sun and Moon (2016); Pokémon Sword and Shield (2019); Pokémon Scarlet and Violet (2022). Each title in that list has its own record in this database with its credited creators and format.

This guide contains facts only. It does not reproduce story text, and it does not claim that any Signature continuation belongs in the official order.
